name: Seoul Dak (서울닭) | Phoenix Marketcity Mumbai
description:
Seoul Dak (서울닭) brings authentic Korean street food flavors to Phoenix Marketcity, Kurla. Dig into crispy Korean Fried Chicken (bone-in and boneless), cheesy Corn Dogs, Dumpling Pops, spicy Tteokbokki, comforting Ramen, and street-style favorites like Rapokki and Crispy Seoul Bowls, perfect for sharing or satisfying a serious comfort-food craving.
Complete your meal with refreshing Bubble Tea, Matcha drinks, and Korean beverages, then treat yourself to desserts like Bingsu and Bungeoppang (the classic Korean fish-shaped dessert). Enjoy a relaxed dine-in experience or grab a quick takeaway, your go-to Korean street food spot inside Phoenix Marketcity, Kurla West.

featured_reviews.review_text: The tteokbokki here hits the spot. It's the perfect balance between hot and sweet. The quantity is filling for one person. featured_reviews.name: Zoya Khan
featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited this place a few months back to have an authentic Korean food experience. Their Tteokbokki was good. The rice cakes had a chew to them and the sauce was spicy.

The corn dog was below average. We ordered for one chicken and one cheese corn dog and they gave us both cheese ones. After bringing it to their staff notice, the staff brought us another cheese corn dog.

Their Korean friend chicken was good but I don’t understand the concept of serving  dumplings with them. If I’m paying almost ₹500 rupees for friend chicken then I expect just chicken no dumplings for filler.

The French fries were decent and crispy.
Their taro bubble tea was forgettable. The staff was friendly but that doesn’t save us from the kind of mediocre food they’d serve.

featured_reviews.name: Adnan Pagarkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
I have lived in Korea so I know Korean food. The waiting to be served was too long.
The "wonton" was missing and had to be reminded.
The staff is clearly untrained, but showed good attitude, mentor them and give them time to pick up.
Management gave my 2 kids 2 gift hampers and this  was very thoughtful and much appreciated.
Below is the review written by my daughter's view point 13 years.

Hope this is taken as improvement.

1. The mozzeralla corn dog was not hot - and very cold. It did not have a cheese pull either as shown in the ad. - it's was very bland, but the breading was good.

2. The Kimchi fries came with seasoning which tasted like basic peri peri seasoning. Not authentic at all. But the fries were hot, crispy and enjoyable

3. The hot and spicy fried chicken was  good. Again, it could have been served warmer- and the spice level could have been reduced. My dad could not handle the spicy. Secondly, the chicken was soggy, and chewy and lacked crispiness. Nonetheless, it was deliciously paired with the potato cuts.

4. The taro bubble tea was delicious and flavourful, with a great Taro aftertaste. The only thing I would recommend is to mention the type of Boba being provided - either popping or chewy Boba.

5. The carbonara tektboki was  delicious, served nice and warm. But- it was slightly chewy, and could have been boiled a little longer, with a thicker sauce, so the rice cakes could have stuck to it.

6. The Mango Bingsu was perfect, delicious and creamy. Just another small recommendation- the fruit used could have been fresh instead of frozen fruit.

featured_reviews.name: Namrata Gaikwad.
featured_reviews.review_text:
The food court at Phoenix Mall is definitely a must-visit for anyone looking for a variety of dining options, whether it's Chinese, Indian, fastfood, or snacks like momos. The mall has a plethora of restaurants ranging from McDonald's, KFC, Subway, Bhagat Chand, and Rajdhani, among many others. Each restaurant is exceptionally clean and well-maintained,which is a big plus point when it comes to dining out.

The food served at all the restaurants tasted exceptional, with each cuisine boasting its unique flavors and spices. The Chinese restaurant served delicious noodles and rice dishes, and the Indian restaurant had a variety of vegetarian and non-vegetarian options. The drinks served here were also refreshing and tasty.

I found the food court an excellent example of a clean and hygienic place, with each restaurant doing their best to provide their customers with the best quality food. The seating arrangements were pretty spacious and comfortable, and the service was prompt.

Overall, I highly recommend the food court at Phoenix Mall if you're looking for good food, hygiene, and comfort. The diversity of cuisines available makes every visit to the food court a unique experience.

If you love spicy street-style food, Zakir Seekh Paratha is definitely worth trying at least once. Their Spicy Seekh Paratha is something you won’t easily find elsewhere – it feels like their own innovation and honestly tastes amazing when cooked properly.

However, one important thing – make sure you clearly tell them to cook the meat well done (red, fully cooked). On our visit, a few pieces were undercooked and we had to send them back.

This place is great to hang out with friends, but I wouldn’t recommend it for a family outing. It’s not among the cleanest food joints, and during rush hours the waiting time can get frustrating. We literally waited around 30 minutes between orders, which really spoiled the flow of our meal.

Overall, amazing taste, unique spicy seekh paratha, but be prepared for delays and give clear cooking instructions before ordering.

featured_reviews.name: All IN ONE
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Flavorful Experience at Vadapav Café – A True Street Food Gem

If you’re someone who loves authentic Indian street food served fresh, with a touch of care and quality, Vadapav Café is a place that should be on your must-visit list. Located in a modest yet inviting stall-style setup, this café manages to capture the essence of Mumbai street flavors while also ensuring that the food is made with 100% groundnut oil — a detail that might seem small but makes a world of difference in taste and health.

From the moment you walk up to the counter, the aroma of freshly fried batata vadas and sizzling bread pakodas hits you. The place is run by people who clearly know and love what they are doing. The staff work quickly but with precision, making sure that every vadapav is perfectly assembled — crisp from the outside, soft and fluffy inside, with chutneys spread just right.

---

Vadapav – The Star of the Show

Let’s start with the classic: the regular Vadapav. At just ₹25, it’s the perfect definition of “value for money.” The pav is lightly toasted, the vada is golden brown and perfectly spiced, and the chutneys (a mix of spicy red chili, tangy tamarind, and fresh green coriander) complement each other beautifully. The first bite is a delightful balance of textures — crunchy, soft, and smooth — and flavors ranging from mildly spicy to tangy and savory.

The Butter Vadapav takes things up a notch. The pav is toasted generously with butter, giving it a richer taste and an indulgent aroma. It’s one of those small upgrades that turns an everyday snack into something you want to savor slowly.

Then comes the Cheese Vadapav. If you’re a cheese lover, this one is pure joy. The molten cheese oozes into every bite, mellowing out the spice while adding creamy depth. And if you’re feeling extra indulgent, the Double Cheese Vadapav is an absolute treat — gooey, rich, and unforgettable.

---

Bread Pakoda – Crispy Comfort Food

If vadapav is the king, the Bread Pakoda is the loyal queen of Indian street snacks. Priced at ₹25 for the regular and ₹40 for the butter version, these are crispy on the outside, soft and flavorful inside, and fried to perfection in groundnut oil, which gives them a clean, non-greasy finish.

For those who can’t resist cheese, the Cheese Bread Pakoda (₹90 for 2 pieces) is heavenly. The melted cheese inside the batter-coated bread, paired with the crunchy crust, is the kind of snack that makes you forget all about counting calories.

featured_reviews.review_text:
A Flavorful Delight: Spicopedia Restaurant Review, Jio World Drive Food Court

I recently visited Spicopedia restaurant in the Jio World Drive food court, and I was blown away by the flavors and authenticity of their dishes. We tried a variety of options, and each one was a winner.

Vada Pav
The Vada Pav was an absolute showstopper - it reminded me of the iconic Ashok Vada Pav from Dadar, and it was absolutely lip-smacking in taste. The vada was crispy on the outside and fluffy on the inside, and the pav was soft and lightly toasted. The combination was pure magic.

Bhel Puri
The Bhel Puri was another delicious option - it was a perfect balance of sweet, spicy, and tangy flavors, with a delightful crunch from the sev and onions.

Paneer Makhni and Dal Makhni with Tandoori Roti
We also tried the Paneer Makhni and Dal Makhni with Tandoori Roti, which were both good options. The paneer was creamy and rich, and the dal was flavorful and comforting. The tandoori roti was soft and lightly charred, perfect for sopping up the sauces.

Service
The service at Spicopedia was friendly and efficient, with our food arriving promptly at our table.

Ambiance
As a food court stall, Spicopedia doesn't have a traditional dining ambiance. However, the stall itself is well-designed and inviting, with a cozy atmosphere that makes you feel like you're in for a treat.

Verdict
Spicopedia restaurant in Jio World Drive's food court is a must-visit for anyone craving authentic and delicious Indian street food. With its lip-smacking Vada Pav, delicious Bhel Puri, and satisfying Paneer Makhni and Dal Makhni, it's a spot that will leave you feeling satisfied and eager to return.

Price: Moderate (around ₹600-₹800 per person)

Recommended for: Foodies, street food lovers, and anyone seeking a delicious and authentic Indian meal.

Will I return?
Absolutely, to try more of Spicopedia's delicious dishes!

featured_reviews.name: Md. Farhan Khan
featured_reviews.review_text:
Had an amazing experience at Baba Falooda, easily one of the most iconic dessert spots in Mumbai for falooda lovers.

The falooda here is absolutely indulgent—rich, creamy, and loaded with everything you’d want. From perfectly cooked sev and sabja seeds to generous scoops of kulfi, ice cream, and dry fruits, every bite feels like a complete dessert experience. Their Baba Special and Royal Malai Falooda are must-tries—both are super filling and packed with flavor.

What really stands out is the consistency and legacy. This place has been around for decades and still manages to pull huge crowds every day, which says a lot about its quality and popularity.

The vibe is very typical Mumbai—busy, slightly chaotic, and always buzzing. Don’t expect a fancy seating setup; most people either stand and enjoy or take it away.

👍 What Works:

Extremely rich & authentic falooda taste

Generous portions (one can easily be shared)

Wide variety of flavors and combinations

Quick service despite heavy crowd

👎 What Could Be Better:

Limited or no proper seating

Can get very crowded, especially in evenings

Slightly heavy on the stomach if you’re not used to rich desserts

---

🧠 Final Verdict:

If you love falooda, this place is a must-visit in Mumbai. It’s not about ambience, it’s about pure dessert satisfaction and nostalgia. One visit and you’ll know why it’s so hyped.
